`LAR-SIDE-REAR-SysArch` — **e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751**. Read-only assessment; no native profile loading or engineering acceptance claimed.

**Preferred first prototype:** a localized barrel-side neck containing the outward S-bend **before the barrel end**, followed by a straight axial bus outside the endcap, with outward turns in the existing rear break. Endcap services should leave through explicitly designed rear ports. This removes the front bend as the gap-setting feature without assuming smaller pipes.

Proposed drawing/screening targets, using local radial/tangential coordinates and \(w=|z|\):

| Element | Initial target and limitation |
|---|---|
| Barrel neck/service box | Reserve **w3000–4000 mm**. A single 100 mm jacket’s conservative radial envelope, including 20 mm clearance, is **R2665.3–3099 mm**. Start with the existing **700 mm ordinary /1100 mm utility tangential lane budgets**, then replace area estimates with individual pipe/cable sweeps. These are proposed reservations. |
| Bend inside that box | Retain R400 mm bends and the 293.7 mm outward displacement: centreline axial span **619.403 mm**, legacy envelope **739.403 mm**. One drawing seed is centreline endpoints **(R2735.3,w3320) → (R3029,w3939.403)**. The first radius remains a proxy pending actual utility/header origins; this seed does not establish containment. |
| External axial bus | **R3029 mm**, continuing beside the endcap to the rear. A straight 100 mm jacket leaves **30 mm** to the R2949 endcap and **51 mm** to the R3130 HCAL apothem. Individual straight pipes fit this screen; the complete station bundle and supports remain unproved. |
| Rear outward turn | Within **w5860–6360 mm**, retain R400 mm. Allowing 20 mm independently at both axial faces requires **490 mm**, leaving only **10 mm**. A screening centreline turn starts near **w5880**, finishes radially outward near **w6280**, then continues through the rear break. Flanges, valves and supports can invalidate this allowance. |
| Exterior handoff | Route radially beyond the HCAL outline. Its 4625.9 mm outer apothem implies approximately **4716.53 mm corner radius**; **R4800 mm** is a useful provisional handoff marker, subject to magnet/yoke and installation clearance. |

The dimensional inputs and existing arithmetic are in [services.json](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/tools/lar_calorimeter/services.json#L29-L61) and [services.py](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/tools/lar_calorimeter/services.py#L46-L58).

The governing failure checks are:

- **A side port followed by an ordinary radial quarter-turn fails.** Its 470 mm one-clearance envelope exceeds the barrel/endcap corridors by **170/289 mm**. The long S-bend must occur within the redesigned neck, rather than being moved unchanged into either narrow corridor.
- **The proposed neck is occupied space.** The band contains H-rings centred at w3250/3750 and board rows near w3000/3500; the route crosses closed cold-wall/vacuum/warm-wall shells. Actual swept paths must determine which supports can be skirted and which boards or boundaries need redesign. There are only **28 spare board slots** above the 3-million-channel planning requirement, so slot removal needs a capacity check. [barrel_services.py, lines34–68](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/tools/lar_calorimeter/barrel_services.py#L34-L68), [DES032, lines132–177](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/docs/design/DES-032-allegro-lar-barrel.md#L132-L177)
- **Rear endcap connectivity is unresolved.** Signal/HV paths encounter the unported support annulus; headers, return circuits and rear penetrations also remain absent. [DES033, lines110–128](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md#L110-L128)
- **An inward endcap shift does not enlarge the full radial exit window.** A 400 mm shift creates 900 mm behind the endcap, but HCAL barrel still ends at5860: unobstructed outward egress remains **5860–6360, 500 mm**. The extra room can house ports/headers inside R3130 unless the HCAL barrel or service pocket is also amended. The collar reservation separately requires redesign. [DES033, lines45–86](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e5e1ecd68bbdcd8c3f9e6402e2089db1c8eab751/docs/design/DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md#L45-L86)

A tangential/3D neck is the fallback. Turning in a tangential–axial plane can reduce radial excursion, but requires a port already oriented appropriately; rotating the drawing does not make a radial-port elbow fit.

Required handoffs: CaloTech owns cold collection, loads and neck/rear ports; SysArch owns the exterior bus, HCAL exit and common-service interfaces; magnet/field, forward-region and software owners must reconcile their boundaries. Preserve all current pipe counts initially.

Actual checks: read pinned inputs, verified all seven supplied SHA-256 hashes, recalculated bend/clearance/capacity bounds, and inspected pinned barrel-shell construction. **No files changed or runtime jobs run.** Next evidence should be one explicit utility-neck sweep plus the complete station layout and rear-port assembly; no reduced front gap is yet validated.

limitations: Only userMessage and agentMessage text retained; reasoning, tool arguments/results and private state excluded.
